verdict.rationale: Reflect publishes a documented public REST API with OAuth 2 (including PKCE) and bearer-token auth. A machine-readable OpenAPI 3.0 spec on openpm, linked from the vendor docs, covers listing graphs, getting and adding links, appending to daily notes, creating notes and reading the current user. The surface is narrow, though: the docs say end-to-end encryption means note contents cannot be served through the API, so a programmatic client can mostly write and append rather than fully drive the product. Missing for 10: read/search access to note contents, broader endpoint coverage (edit, delete, tags, search), a versioning or deprecation policy, a sandbox or test environment, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: For authentication, we support OAuth 2. You will need to create credentials here.
Our supports appending data to your notes, returning a list of the links you've bookmarked, and a few other things.
We do support OAuth's PKCE extension which means you can build a client to Reflect without shipping secret keys around.
Your notes contents are end-to-end encrypted. Our servers can't read the contents of your notes, so we can't serve them up in the API.
